{{short description|Finnish botanist (1931-)}}
'''Leena Hämet-Ahti''' (née Hämet, b. 3 January 1931, [[Kuusamo]]), also known as '''Raija-Leena Hämet-Ahti''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hämet-Ahti, Raija-Leena {{!}} International Plant Names Index |url=https://www.ipni.org/a/3533-1 |access-date=2026-05-08 |website=www.ipni.org}}</ref> is a Finnish [[botanist]], [[plant taxonomist]], and [[plant collector]] noted for being Associate Professor of Botany at the [[University of Helsinki]], and later the Director of the university's Botanical Garden.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goward |first1=Trevor |title=TEUVO AHTI AND LEENA HÄMET-AHTI: A WELLS GRAY HONEYMOON |url=https://www.ou.edu/cas/botany-micro/ben/ben436.html |website=www.ou.edu |publisher=Botanical Electronic News - 436 |accessdate=18 February 2019 |quote=Leena Hämet-Ahti and Teuvo (Ted) Ahti are familiar friends to western Canadian botany. Residents of Finland, Leena was Associate Professor of Botany at the University of Helsinki (later also Director of the university's Botanical Garden), while Ted was Professor of Cryptogamic Botany (later also [[Academy Professor]]) at the same university. Beginning in 1958 and 1961, respectively, Ted and Leena made numerous forays to western North America, especially British Columbia, ultimately amassing c. 10,500 specimens from this region. Most of this material is deposited at the Finnish Natural History Museum}}</ref>  

== Biography ==
She primarily studies alpine plants of Finland and similar northern hemisphere climates.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tiedenaisia - Vetenskapskvinnor - Women of Learning |url=http://www.helsinki.fi/akka-info/tiedenaiset/english/hamet_ahti.html |website=www.helsinki.fi |accessdate=18 February 2019 |quote=Leena Hämet-Ahti has studied the bioclimatic vegetation zones of the northern hemisphere, especially areas similar to Finland on the northern coniferous zone.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hämet-Ahti: Villiruusuista-1 |url=http://www.ruususeura.fi/a-suomi/artikkelit/hamet-ahti/villiruusuista-1.html |website=www.ruususeura.fi |accessdate=18 February 2019 |language=Finnish}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Frodin |first1=David G. |title=Guide to Standard Floras of the World: An Annotated, Geographically Arranged Systematic Bibliography of the Principal Floras, Enumerations, Checklists and Chorological Atlases of Different Areas |date=2001 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9781139428651 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aMjXCF4rmDUC&pg=PA613 |accessdate=18 February 2019 |language=en}}</ref> Her PhD thesis, defended in 1963, was on mountain birch forests.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Zonation of the mountain birch forests in northernmost Fennoscandia|author=Leena Hämet-Ahti|year=1963| journal=Annales Botanici Societatis Zoologicae Botanicae Fennicae "Vanamo" |volume=34 |issue=4 |pages=1–127 }}</ref> She participated in the production of the seminal Finnish [[Flora (publication)|floras]] ''Retkeilykasvio'' (1984, 1998) and ''Suomen puu- ja pensaskasvio'' (1992).

Hämet-Ahti won the  [[Finnish Cultural Foundation]] prize in 1990<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skr.fi/default.asp?docId=12900|title=Keskusrahaston palkinnot|website=Suomen kulttuurirahasto| accessdate=5 May 2012}}</ref>  and the {{ill|Finnish Biological Society Vanamo|fi|Suomen Biologian Seura Vanamo}} silver Kairamo medal in 2007 "in recognition of her many merits in botany, university teaching, science popularisation and fostering Finnish cultural heritage".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vanamo.fi/m_mitalit2004.html|title=Vanamon mitalit|website=Suomen biologian seura Vanamo|accessdate=5 May 2012|archive-date=5 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305042909/http://www.vanamo.fi/m_mitalit2004.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her book ''Maarianheinä, mesimarja ja timotei'' won a {{ill|State Public Information Award|fi|Tiedonjulkistamisen valtionpalkinto}} in 1987 and her ''Suomen puu- ja pensaskasvio'' was selected as {{ill|Science Book of the Year|fi|vuoden tiedekirja}} in 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tsv.fi/vtk/arkisto.htm|title=Vuoden tiedekirjat|accessdate=5 May 2012|archive-date=13 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121013165902/http://www.tsv.fi/vtk/arkisto.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

Hämet-Ahti has been a member of the [[Finnish Academy of Science and Letters]] since 1991.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.acadsci.fi/jasenet/varsinaiset_jasenet.htm | title = Suomalaisen Tiedeakatemian varsinaiset jäsenet | date = 2 September 2014 | publisher = Suomalainen Tiedeakatemia | accessdate = 2 July 2015 | language = fi | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150808063536/http://www.acadsci.fi/jasenet/varsinaiset_jasenet.htm | archive-date = 8 August 2015 | url-status = dead }}</ref> She is married to botanist and [[lichenologist]] [[Teuvo Ahti]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.waysofenlichenment.net/wells/ahti | title = Teuvo Ahti and Leenä Hämet-Ahti: A Wells Gray Honeymoon | publisher = Ways of Enlichenment | author = Goward, Trevor | accessdate = 12 August 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Smith |first=Val |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q132874317 |title=Common Ground: Who's who in New Zealand botanical names. Supplement Two: Who's who in New Zealand botanical names. Supplement Two |date=2023-01-01 |language=English}}</ref>
